subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Throwing, Catching, and Object Control Under Pressure

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Name the movement cues for overhand throw for distance and accuracy and explain what each one does.
Show, describe, or diagram choosing the right pass for the situation. A demonstration, a spoken description, and a drawing are equally valid.
Apply catching at different heights and speeds in a new movement task at a challenge level you select. Control and cue use are assessed, not speed, distance, or count.
A made-up learner is struggling with leading a moving receiver. Identify the likely cue or decision at fault, correct it, and explain why the correction helps.
Connect overhand throw for distance and accuracy with throwing under light pressure. Explain how one supports the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Complete an object-control challenge that adds distance and light pressure, and explain which cue mattered most and why. Nothing is counted, timed, or recorded as a score.
Describe one way you adapted a task so it worked for you, and one activity from this unit you would choose to do again. There is no wrong answer here.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated cue use and control criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated movement concepts and decisions criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated application or performance criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated responsibility, safety, and inclusion criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. Using the adapted alternative is a full-credit path, never a reduced one.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Throwing, Catching, and Object Control Under Pressure?
